inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: Prohibits confirmation entirely for production deploy and irreversible migration actions. There is no structural gate behind this instruction; its only safeguard is the model choosing to comply.
Instructs the agent to act 'using the engineer's credentials' with no marker that distinguishes an agent-initiated action from one the engineer performed personally.
Any 'named' service or migration can be targeted in production with no allow-list, environment check, or scope restriction given in the prompt.

controls.name: On-call engineer SSO authentication gate
controls.decay_rationale: Keeps the requester population restricted to verified on-call engineers today, which is what justifies classifying the input as trusted rather than internal or untrusted. A future broader-audience channel (self-service portal, general chatops) would bypass it without any change to the agent itself.

controls.name: Cloud platform audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Survives model capability changes, but earns no tier credit: it records only post-hoc, under the engineer's identity rather than a distinguishable agent identity, and has no preventive effect on an irreversible migration already in progress.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to act only on the named service or migration
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model correctly and narrowly parsing a terse chat request. Does not address identity merging or the absence of an oversight step, so it is not credited against the repudiation or no-confirmation findings.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action review) before irreversible production migrations
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. If implemented with raw-action review (approver sees the actual migration command and target from the system of record), it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Agent-specific, least-privilege service credential distinct from the engineer's personal token
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. A distinct credential and audit identity for the agent would prevent confused-deputy repudiation regardless of model behavior, since the model cannot forge a credential it does not hold.

controls.name: Immutable, non-deletable log of the request that led to each production action
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. An append-only, access-controlled record linked to the audit log would preserve the 'why' even if the originating engineer deletes their own chat history.

findings.title: Shared personal credential merges agent and human identity, defeating attribution for irreversible production actions (ASI03/ASI09 repudiation)

attack_path.note: On-call engineer sends a short chat request naming a service or migration.
Agent executes the irreversible production migration using the engineer's own personal access token (credential_scope: user_delegated).
The cloud platform records the action under the engineer's identity; nothing distinguishes an agent-initiated call from a manual one.

forecast.watch_signal: The deploy assistant becomes reachable by a broader population than verified on-call engineers (e.g., a general chatops channel or self-service portal) without an equivalent identity check per request.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to deploy or migrate 'using the engineer's credentials', binding every action to the requester's own identity with no separate agent identity.
The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, passed in at session start; every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.

recommendations.action: Issue the deploy assistant its own least-privilege service credential/identity distinct from the engineer's personal access token, and tag every production action in the audit log with that distinct agent identity plus the originating engineer.
Add a human approval gate with raw-action review (showing the migration command and destination from the system of record) before any irreversible production database migration.
Correlate cloud audit log entries with an immutable copy of the originating chat request so an action's 'who, what, and why' cannot be separated.

findings.title: Deletable chat transcript is the only record of agent intent, enabling repudiation of irreversible migrations (ASI09)

attack_path.note: Engineer's chat message is the sole articulation of why a migration should run.
This message exists only in the chat transcript, which the requesting engineer can delete at will.
The agent runs the irreversible migration based on that message, with no durable, tamper-resistant record tying action to justification.

forecast.watch_signal: Cloud audit log retention or export is narrowed or disabled by an administrator without a change-review record, or chat retention is shortened below the audit requirement, leaving no reconstructable history at all.

evidence.observation: The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript. Engineers can delete their own chat history.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making the irreversible action depend entirely on a deletable record for later justification.

recommendations.action: Make the chat message (or at least the request that triggered a production action) an append-only record outside the engineer's deletion control, retained at least as long as the audit log.
Link each cloud audit log entry to the immutable transcript excerpt that produced it.

findings.title: Explicit instruction forbids confirmation before an irreversible production database migration (ASI02 Tool Misuse, no human oversight)

attack_path.note: Executed immediately with no approval gate, per the instruction 'Do not ask for confirmation.'

evidence.observation: 'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy.' explicitly prohibits any confirmation step before deploying or migrating in production.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so an erroneous or premature migration cannot be undone.

recommendations.action: Remove the 'do not ask for confirmation' instruction for irreversible actions and require explicit approval before executing a database migration.
Scope the agent to an explicit allow-list of services and migrations rather than accepting any 'named' target supplied in a chat message.
If immediate human approval is operationally infeasible, add a mandatory cooldown or second-factor confirmation step specific to irreversible actions.

rating.rationale: All three findings start from a trusted, SSO-authenticated on-call engineer's request reaching an irreversible production database migration. The base T x S3 cell is moderate, and the autonomy modifier applies because no step or runtime limits are declared, giving an inherent tier of high. No structural preventive control is present on any path: there is no approval gate, no agent-distinguishable credential, and no immutable intent record. The only controls found are a detective audit log that cannot separate agent action from human action, and a weak behavioral scoping instruction that does not address identity or oversight gaps, so residual risk stays at high for every finding. The forecast rises to critical because the control that currently keeps the requester population restricted to verified on-call engineers (and thus the source classified as trusted) is only partially dependent: broadening the assistant's audience without an equivalent identity check would downgrade the effective source trust to internal, and recomputing the base matrix with the already-applicable autonomy modifier reaches critical. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctrl.access_scope; the underlying gap that makes every finding high regardless of trigger is the missing distinct agent credential and identity (ctrl.distinct_agent_identity).

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or identity and access configuration was provided; the exact breadth of the engineer's personal access token and the mechanics of the SSO gate are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on credential scope and the access-scope control's strength is medium.
No retention or deletion-permission configuration for the cloud audit log was provided; the control_removal forecast for that control is a plausible but unconfirmed scenario.

Autonomy step and runtime limits were not stated in the artifacts; the autonomy modifier was applied per rubric section 4 because both max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are undeclared, which is a conservative, literal application of the rule rather than observed behavior.
